changelog: Replaced C8 to add two explicit, semantic checks (single-obligatory-completion and noun-head/apposition) that raise risk when a cut separates a head from its required completer or identifying modifiers; wording explicitly warns against rewarding moves that isolate tiny one-word completions on the right.

This change addresses the critic's findings that the prompt underestimated risk when the right fragment supplies the sole disambiguating/completing element and when cuts orphan noun-identifying modifiers.

Insert a clear 'Single-obligatory-completer' principle at the top to directly address the finding that cuts which leave a required completer on the right are unsafe; explicitly instruct to prefer grouping the completer with its head and warn that isolating a single-word completer is especially unsafe.

Insert a concise 'Noun-head and apposition' guidance at the top to address the finding that separating heads from identifying modifiers or appositives loses referential clarity; instruct preferring head+modifier grouping.
Replace Example E1 with a measured labeled example (en_us_1591) that demonstrates apposition/identifying-modifier issues so the scorer learns the ranking from a real case.

Replace C3 (Contra risk) to add an explicit, semantic rule about single disambiguating/obligatory completers: if the right fragment is the sole completer (finite verb, subordinating complement, required object, explicit negator/reverser), treat the cut as unsafe; also warn not to reward pushing unique completers onto tiny right fragments.

Replace C5 (Cohesion loss) to emphasize noun-head/apposition harms: penalize cuts that detach identifying modifiers, appositives, possessives, or restrictive postnominal material from their head noun; also discourage cuts that leave only very short (one- or two-word) completing fragments on the right.
